solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This rifleman's a one-off, wrinkly dog

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so a letter drops away from the breed name

parts.note: the shar-pei is a Chinese breed famous for its deeply folded skin
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A wry description of a soldier as a one-of-a-kind, crumpled old dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-off' looks like a single word meaning unique, but splits into one (I) and off. Richard Sharpe is Bernard Cornwell's rifleman hero of the Napoleonic wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpe is the fictional green-jacketed soldier of Cornwell's novels, serving in the 95th Rifles.

clue.text: An author's nightmare about capsizing

parts.note: a nightmarish experience is hell

indicators.note: a boat that capsizes turns upside down, so in a down clue the letters flip

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A writer's worst dream: being on a boat as it overturns.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Heller wrote Catch-22. 'About' looks like part of the phrase 'about capsizing', but it supplies RE before being overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Heller was an American novelist and satirist, so he is one example of a writer.

clue.text: Work by Clavell, not King or Grass

indicators.note: not means without, so a word is dropped from the title

parts.note: King Rat is James Clavell's novel set in a Japanese prison camp
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A note listing which of James Clavell's books something is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like another title to rule out, but it is the definition: in British slang to grass is to inform on someone, and an informer is a grass or a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for an informer who betrays associates to the police.

clue.text: She visits Golden Pond before the lakeside stores

indicators.note: to store is to keep inside, so the run of words holds the name within it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A woman calls at Golden Pond before going on to the shops by the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: On Golden Pond is Ernest Thompson's play, filmed with Katharine Hepburn, about an elderly couple who spend summers at their lake cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel Thayer is the wife who returns each summer to the lakeside cottage in On Golden Pond.

clue.text: Who wrote Amelia's line in German?

parts.note: a line of work or study is a field
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A question about who penned one of Amelia's lines in the German language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amelia's line' reads as a line of dialogue, but the 's is 'is' and the line is a field of activity. Henry Fielding's Amelia (1751) was his last novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding, author of Tom Jones, published the novel Amelia in 1751.

clue.text: Nurse pinches bottom of popular novelist

indicators.note: to pinch something is to grip it between the fingers, so one piece is squeezed inside another

parts.note: to nurse or foster is to nurture and bring up

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cheeky nurse gives a well-loved author a pinch on the behind.
explanation.walkthrough: E. M. Forster wrote A Passage to India and Howards End. 'Nurse' looks like a noun, a person doing the pinching, but it works as the verb foster.
explanation.definitionFit: E. M. Forster was an English writer of fiction, author of A Room with a View.

clue.text: Fateful day for Brussels bureaucrats? Kindly ones?

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union
the bureaucrats are simply men, as in EU men
the Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was assassinated

explanation.surface: Asks what doom awaits the EU's officials, then wonders whether they are kindly people.
explanation.walkthrough: The day comes 'for' the EU men, so it goes after them. The Eumenides are the Furies of Greek myth, given a flattering euphemistic name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek name Eumenides literally means the well-disposed or gracious ones, a placating title for the avenging Furies.

clue.text: He wrote On the Marriage of a Virgin: sadly, a month out

definitions.text: He wrote On the Marriage of a Virgin

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note that the poet of a wedding poem sadly is away for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' reads as a comment on the absence, but it is part of the fodder. On the Marriage of a Virgin is a 1941 poem by the Welsh poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas, the Welsh poet of Under Milk Wood, wrote the poem On the Marriage of a Virgin.

clue.text: Recently arrived, one out of one's seat

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of place, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
in anatomy natal means relating to the nates, the buttocks, on which one sits

explanation.surface: Someone who has just turned up and is already up out of their chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of one's seat' reads as a single idiom for standing up, but it splits: out signals the shuffle of one, and 'of one's seat' is the rare anatomical sense of natal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal describes a newborn infant in its first weeks, someone who has only just come into the world.

clue.text: One of the King's Men who could put an end to a quarrel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Jacobean playwright who wrote for Shakespeare's acting company, the King's Men

definitions.text: who could put an end to a quarrel
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a maker of arrows, who fits feathers to the end of a crossbow bolt, called a quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a royal peacemaker, but a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, and an arrow maker finishes its end with feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname comes from the trade of arrow making, and John Fletcher succeeded Shakespeare as house dramatist.

clue.text: The first to make cheese? There's no way he was a poet!

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

indicators.note: no means without, so the following abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: Stilton is a blue English cheese
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone asks who first made cheese, then scoffs that he could never have been a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's no way' reads as scornful disbelief, but it instructs dropping a street from the cheese. John Milton wrote Paradise Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton, the seventeenth-century author of Paradise Lost, is among the greatest English poets.

clue.text: Like the story of the lost child's ice cream

definitions.text: Like the story of the lost child
definitions.meaning: first meaning: The Story of the Lost Child is the last of Elena Ferrante's novels set in Naples
second meaning: the three-flavoured striped block of ice cream

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sad tale about a child's dessert, but the story is Ferrante's novel, the fourth of her Naples quartet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things from Naples, which includes Ferrante's quartet, and names the striped strawberry, vanilla and chocolate ice-cream brick.

clue.text: Mate holding out pints ordered after the match

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it within your grasp, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a mate is a friend, a pal

indicators.note: things ordered are arranged into a sequence, so these letters get a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend handing round pints bought after the football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting fixture, but it is a marriage; 'out' reads as handing round drinks, though it is just part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A match can mean a marriage, and postnuptial describes whatever happens following a wedding.

clue.text: Writer holding back a tide

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters run right to left
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author trying, like King Canute, to hold the sea back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' wants to be a person, but here it is the instrument; 'holding back' reads as one phrase but splits into two instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap is the type of tide with the smallest range, occurring at the moon's first and last quarters.

clue.text: I share bed with Jude after his first break-up

definitions.text: I share bed with Jude after his first break-up

indicators.note: what remains after the first letter is everything except the opening one
breaking something up scatters its pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the name without its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman confesses she now sleeps with Jude, after his marriage broke down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: in Hardy's Jude the Obscure, Sue lives with Jude after his marriage to Arabella collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue Bridehead is Jude Fawley's cousin and lover in Thomas Hardy's novel, cohabiting with him unmarried.

clue.text: Eliot's village festival involves endless drink

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap something in, so one piece lies inside another

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut

parts.note: Coke, short for Coca-Cola, is a soft drink

explanation.surface: A village fête at T. S. Eliot's home that features a bottomless drink.
explanation.walkthrough: East Coker, in Somerset, is the second of Eliot's Four Quartets and the village where his ashes lie.
explanation.definitionFit: East Coker is the Somerset village of Eliot's ancestors, which gives its name to one of his Four Quartets.

clue.text: The Joads left this city house after consent by mother

indicators.note: after places what precedes it later in the sequence, so the earlier clue words are written second

parts.note: to give your OK is to consent
LA is Los Angeles
HO is the abbreviation for house
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: The Joad family quit their town home once mother agreed to it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Steinbeck's The Grapes of Wrath the Joads leave their Dust Bowl farm for California; 'after consent' places the city and house behind OK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grapes of Wrath follows the Joad family's migration west from the drought-stricken US state to California.

clue.text: A writer almost bagging another's piles of dosh

indicators.note: to bag something is to pocket it or put it in a sack, so letters go inside
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons
Stephen King is another writer; with the possessive he becomes KING'S

explanation.surface: One author nearly pocketing another author's heaps of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The enclosure goes straight after the leading A, splitting A from the shortened surname. Dosh is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an enormous sum, as much as would be demanded to free a captured monarch.

clue.text: An island gathering shot Portia's suitor

indicators.note: to gather something is to draw it in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland
to have a shot is to have a go

explanation.surface: A crowd on an island fires at the man courting Portia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' looks like a noun meaning a crowd, but it is the verb. The Prince of Arragon fails Portia's casket test in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Merchant of Venice the Prince of Arragon woos Portia but chooses the silver casket and loses.

clue.text: Harding's one in conflict then retreat

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Someone's soldier is in combat and then falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harding's one' means Harding is one: Septimus Harding is the title character of Trollope's The Warden, warden of Hiram's Hospital almshouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Harding holds the post of keeper of an almshouse for old men in Trollope's first Barchester novel.

clue.text: A nurse who drinks this used to stay dry

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the gin-loving midwife-nurse Sarah in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit
second meaning: a large umbrella, named after the one she always carries

explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies a nurse who drinks something to stay sober; 'this used to stay dry' is a separate meaning, an object you hold over your head in rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's tipsy nurse carried a bulky umbrella, and her surname became British slang for that article.

clue.text: Public schoolboy's haircut's an aberration

indicators.note: an aberration departs from the normal course, so these letters stray from their order

parts.note: taken as written, with the S of the possessive
taken as written; it doubles as the start of the signal phrase

explanation.surface: A private-school pupil's hairstyle is an odd mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: A Carthusian is a pupil at Charterhouse, a British fee-paying public school in Surrey. Note that the British 'public school' means an elite private one.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse takes its Latin name from the Carthusian monastery on whose site it was founded, so its pupils bear that name.

clue.text: God of the Dawn sounds less cold

indicators.note: less means minus, so a letter is subtracted

parts.note: a chorus is sounds made by many voices together
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: The god of morning seems to be less chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' looks like a homophone signal, but it is a noun, as in the dawn chorus of birdsong. Horus is the falcon-headed Egyptian sky god.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus, the Egyptian falcon god, was associated with the rising sun at daybreak.

clue.text: A preface to Bear Island

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word that comes before bear in the name of the huge Alaskan brown bear
second meaning: the large island off southern Alaska

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the introduction to Alistair MacLean's novel Bear Island, but a preface here is just a word placed before another.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alaskan island gives its name to a giant subspecies of brown bear found there.

clue.text: A Queen's become abusive about another

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is surrounded by the rest

parts.note: to get angry is to become angry
abusive language is rude
another queen: R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A royal lady has turned insulting about a rival monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' points back to Queen, so it means another queen, R. Gertrude is Hamlet's mother, Queen of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude is the queen of Denmark in Shakespeare's Hamlet, married to Claudius after her husband's murder.

clue.text: Part of a Manhattan schoolboy's dream workplace?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the whiskey that is the base of a Manhattan cocktail
second meaning: Salinger's Holden Caulfield dreams of standing in a field of this grain, catching children before they fall off a cliff

explanation.walkthrough: 'Manhattan schoolboy' reads as one phrase about Holden Caulfield, which is a decoy; the Manhattan is the cocktail and the boy stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye whiskey is the classic spirit in the cocktail, and a rye field is where Salinger's narrator imagines working as the catcher.

clue.text: Steer around Burns's old river vessel

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its steering
auld is Scots for old, as in Burns's Auld Lang Syne
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Guide an old boat along a river that Robert Burns knew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River vessel' reads as one phrase meaning a boat, but splits: river is R, and vessel alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is a large metal cooking pot, and a pot is a container, a common sense of vessel.

clue.text: An author's relentless energy

parts.note: stern means strict and unyielding
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A writer is praised for his tireless drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy. 'Relentless energy' reads as a single phrase but it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century Anglo-Irish novelist and clergyman, so he is a writer.
